prerequisites: Distributed generation systems and power quality (Semester 2)

learning_outcomes.text: Possess and understand knowledge that provides a basis or opportunity for originality in the development and/or application of ideas, often in a research context.
That students know how to apply acquired knowledge and problem-solving skills in new or unfamiliar environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their area of study.

That students are able to integrate knowledge and face the complexity of making judgments based on information that, being incomplete or limited, includes reflections on the social and ethical responsibilities linked to the application of their knowledge and judgments.
That students know how to communicate their conclusions and the ultimate knowledge and reasons that support them to specialized and non-specialized audiences in a clear and unambiguous way.
That students possess the learning skills that will enable them to continue studying in a way that will be largely self-directed or autonomous.

Write, interpret scientifically and communicate orally, to specialized audiences, documents in the field of the master's master lines (electric power systems, electric and hybrid vehicles, energy efficiency and renewable energies).
Identify the aspects of technical design that depend to a greater extent on strategic, socio-political, economic and environmental conditioning factors.
Skills related to teamwork, recognizing different roles within a group and different ways of organizing research teams.
Ability to manage information: search, analysis and synthesis of the specific technical information.
Ability to assimilate and communicate information in English concerning technical
Ability to plan and organize work
Skills for critical reasoning, making decisions and making judgments based on information that include reflecting on social and ethical responsibilities of professional activity
Skills for initiative, entreprenourship, quality and results achievements
Understand the importance and scope of use of electrical power systems.
Identify and locate the different geopolitical regions that make up the current world and describe their main economic features, in relation to primary energy sources.

Knowing and analyzing the energy structures and technologies that allow assuring the coverage of the determined demand, analyzing the future energy needs and the possible technological solutions, considering criteria of efficiency, security, guarantee of supply and environmental implications.
Developing an adequate management strategy according to the different offers of the electricity market traders.
Identify the agents participating in the electricity and gas market, as well as their operation considering different management methodologies.
Understanding the price formation process, understanding the different components of the final price of electricity and tariffs.
Assessing the social and environmental implications of the operation of electricity markets.
Explain and analyze the main macroeconomic variables involved in the Spanish and European energy sector.
Define the economic structure of the energy market.
Analyze from the economic point of view the value chain in the different energy businesses.
Analyze the functioning of the Iberian electricity market and assess its relationship with the energy transport capacity in the interconnections.
Recognize the main characteristics of the regulations applicable to accounting.
Define and differentiate the main aspects and business strategies related to investments, financing, risk management and taxation in the energy markets.
Know and classify the main aspects and business strategies related to investments, financing, risk management and taxation in the energy markets.
Apply the acquired financial knowledge to the analysis of investment projects in renewable and conventional energy.

syllabus_topics: Macroeconomic analysis of the energy sector.
Economic analysis of the value chain in the oil, gas and electricity businesses.
Valuation methodologies. Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) valuation
Case study: valuing a wind farm project
teaching_methods: Computer aid tools for problem resolution
assessment_rules: For this subject, students will be evaluated according to percentages for written exam (15% to 40%), oral exams (15% to 40%), works and projects (20% to 50%), practical cases (10% to 30%), and observation techniques (10% to 20%). The exact percentages will be specified at the beginning of the sessions. For differentiated assessment, each case will be studied, and a compatible assessment proposed according to specific conditions and University rules.
